shots.prompt: A panoramic view of a dusty mountain pass at dawn, battered supply trucks rolling forward past weary survivors; the captain stands in the lead truck, scanning the ridgeline.
Close-up of the captain barking orders into a field radio, eyes darting toward the smoke rising behind the convoy.
The aide calmly works the controls of the lead truck as explosions burst along the far slope.
The captain raises a fist and shouts a rallying cry to the soldiers huddled behind the trucks.
The aide crouches by the radio set, turning dials with a deadpan expression as static crackles.
A wide shot of distant artillery flashes lighting the valley as the convoy pushes on through drifting smoke and dust.
The captain ducks behind a boulder and peers over it with exaggerated caution while shells whistle overhead.
An airstrike called in over the radio slams into the positions on the opposite ridge, throwing up towering plumes of dirt and fire.
The captain straightens his greatcoat and strides forward, acting as if he planned the strike all along.
The aide waves the trucks forward through the gap, carrying the field radio on his back.
The captain walks past the wounded resting beside the road, giving each a confident nod that hides his relief.
The aide hands the captain a dented tin mug of tea without a word, still watching the road as medics hurry past.
The captain sips the tea, grimaces at the taste, then salutes the passing column.
A long column of soldiers in grey greatcoats marches along the ridge, silhouetted against the rising sun.
The captain looks back over the battlefield, a flicker of doubt crossing his face before the confident mask returns.
The aide packs up the radio and follows the captain toward the waiting trucks, unimpressed as ever.
A weathered parchment note appears on screen over the mountain pass, closing the story with a dry remark about duty.
